record.title: Pino Hachado and Icalma reported closure during Chilean customs strike, May 2017
record.scope: Named international land crossings Pino Hachado and Icalma; not the whole Argentina–Chile frontier
record.direction: Motorists on Argentine approach at Pino Hachado were reportedly told to return. Bilateral scope and Icalma direction unresolved.
record.movement: Pino Hachado motorists reported turned back; Icalma described unavailable. Full nationality, passenger/freight and directional categories not established.
record.exceptions: ANFACH stated exceptional emergency shifts continued nationally. Customs reported priority cargo contingency; local exemptions at these two posts not established.
record.imposing_authority: Striking Chilean customs personnel (ANFACH); Argentine Gendarmería reported redirecting motorists
record.enforcement: LM Neuquén quotes Escuadrón Las Lajas on actual turnbacks; Río Negro quotes Vialidad Nacional that both passes were unavailable for non-road-condition reasons. No direct researcher observation.
record.relationship: No matching May 2017 customs-strike event or Pino Hachado/Icalma lead found in current629-event/271-lead register.
record.status_observation: Contemporaneous May 2017 evidence only; no present-status inference.
record.official_rationale: ANFACH attributed strike to disputed staffing and career-reclassification commitments. Chilean Customs sought to maintain traffic through contingency staffing.
record.context: Intentional strike-related interruption of border processing; concrete motorist turnbacks attributed to Gendarmería at Pino Hachado. Same/next-day opening reports are preserved.
record.uncertainty: DiarioAndino May 24 headline lists Pino Hachado open; Río Negro May 25 reports open posts and says strike did not cause regional closures, while DiarioAndino May 25 still calls Pino Hachado/Icalma strike total. Exact within-day chronology and end remain unresolved. National strike-end reports conflict (May 29 versus June 2) and cannot establish local closure endpoints.

historical.duration_note: Local continuity and exact endpoint unresolved; root must not calculate.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Specific motorist turnbacks and named-post unavailability reported through Argentine agencies; contrary same/next-day opening accounts retained.
Two May 24 contemporaneous reports describe interruption already occurring that morning; no precise operational first refusal time inferred.
May 25 open report is not an exact reopening and conflicts with total-strike report; national end claims May 29 andJune2 cannot supply local endpoint.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded rationale and claim assessment support the selected subcategories. All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Labor staffing/reclassification grievance supported; none of six rationale codes directly established. Trade affected does not establish protectionist motive.
Pino Hachado and Icalma named; direct motorist return claim only Pino Hachado. Samoré delays and other open posts excluded. Local emergency/freight exceptions unresolved.
Conflicting local reports and national contingency operations rule out assuming a single uninterrupted strike-length closure.
